# ASVS 5.0.0 L2: V10 OAuth and OIDC

<!-- Generated by `pnpm security:asvs --write` from the YAML file next to this one. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Self-assessment against OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, Level 2, chapter V10 OAuth and OIDC: not yet assessed by a person. The entries below are the working state, filled in with tests and code pointers; the maintainer's first pass and second pass are still to come. This is not a certification, and no independent party has reviewed it. OWASP does not certify projects.

Status: **in progress**. 8 pass, 21 n/a, 0 fail.

| **10.1.1** Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them. For example, when using a backend-for-frontend pattern for browser-based JavaScript applications, access and refresh tokens shall only be accessible for the backend. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-10.1.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts) | Server-side code flow: only the id_token is read from the token response, verified and discarded; the access token and any refresh token are never stored, forwarded or logged, and the browser gets only the opaque session cookie. The client secret goes only to the token endpoint. |
| **10.1.2** Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server (such as the authorization code or ID Token) if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction. This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the proof key for code exchange (PKCE) 'code_verifier', 'state' or OIDC 'nonce', are not guessable, are specific to the transaction, and are securely bound to both the client and the user agent session in which the transaction was started. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-10.1.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/login-state.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/login-state.ts) | State, nonce and PKCE verifier are random per login, stored hashed, single use, and tied to the browser by the login cookie. Two parallel logins in one browser share the cookie and one fails closed (ADR-0011). |
| **10.2.1** Verify that, if the code flow is used, the OAuth client has protection against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which trigger token requests, either by using proof key for code exchange (PKCE) functionality or checking the 'state' parameter that was sent in the authorization request. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-10.2.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts) | The client sends a PKCE S256 challenge and checks a single-use state bound to the browser. The first test asserts the challenge, state and nonce in the authorization URL, not that the verifier reaches the token endpoint (the test provider does not check it; backlog); the state checks are what the tests prove. The browser journey apps/web/e2e/oidc.spec.ts runs the whole flow through the web app against a provider on a local port whose token endpoint checks the code verifier against the S256 challenge it was given and answers invalid_grant otherwise: the sign-in, the sign-in again for a change that needs a recent authentication, and the start of a link all succeed, so the verifier does reach the token endpoint, and the test reads the last authorization request (S256, a nonce, a state, prompt=login and max_age=0 for the re-authentication). |
| **10.2.2** Verify that, if the OAuth client can interact with more than one authorization server, it has a defense against mix-up attacks. For example, it could require that the authorization server return the 'iss' parameter value and validate it in the authorization response and the token response. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-10.2.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc-provider.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc-provider.ts) | The defence is per-provider: a callback URL per provider, a state tied to the provider that started it, the code sent only to that provider's token endpoint, and an id_token iss check. | **10.3.1** Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service (audience). | **10.3.2** Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization. | **10.3.3** Verify that if an access control decision requires identifying a unique user from an access token (JWT or related token introspection response), the resource server identifies the user from claims that cannot be reassigned to other users. | **10.4.2** Verify that, if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response, it can be used only once for a token request. | **10.4.4** Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs to use. Note that the grants 'token' (Implicit flow) and 'password' (Resource Owner Password Credentials flow) must no longer be used. | L1 | n/a |  | Restricting the grant types of a client is an authorization server function. | **10.4.5** Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients, preferably using sender-constrained refresh tokens, i.e., Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) or Certificate-Bound Access Tokens using mutual TLS (mTLS). If refresh token rotation is used, the authorization server must invalidate the refresh token after usage, and revoke all refresh tokens for that authorization if an already used and invalidated refresh token is provided. | L1 | n/a |  | Mitigating refresh token replay is an authorization server duty. Scorpion stores and uses no refresh token: only the id_token is read from the token response. |
| **10.4.6** Verify that, if the code grant is used, the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring proof key for code exchange (PKCE). For a token request, it must require validation of the 'code_verifier' parameter. | L2 | n/a |  | Requiring PKCE and refusing the plain method is enforced by the authorization server; Scorpion is the client that sends S256 (see 10.2.1) and cannot enforce anything on the server. |
